=== Usage Dashboard replaces the Usage Report

The Usage Dashboard is now available to organization admins in the *Usage* category of Analytics Reports. It replaces the previous Usage Report.

* Filter by date range and, optionally, by team.
* Review totals for sessions, minutes, devices used, and active users.
* Review session counts by type and date, and usage statistics for each team.
* See top users and most-used devices ranked by testing minutes, with each user or device listed once and all of its teams shown in the *Team* column.
* Export the dashboard as a CSV file.

// Source: KOB-56666 from PR #986
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/986

== deviceConnect

- Updated the nginx web server bundled with deviceConnect on macOS host machines to version 1.30.7. This version addresses security vulnerabilities published by the nginx project for version 1.30.4. The update is installed automatically when a host machine is upgraded to this deviceConnect release. No configuration changes are required, and existing nginx settings are preserved. Linux host machines aren't affected because they use the nginx package provided by the operating system.

// Source: KOB-56322 from PR #985
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/985

== Inspector data available after a slow app launch

In iOS and Android automation sessions, inspector data is no longer lost for the rest of the session when an app is slow to start.

Previously, after a script launched or relaunched an app that took a long time to start, most later steps in Session Explorer showed "There is no inspection data available for this screenshot." until the session ended. Now, only the steps captured while the app is not responding have no inspector data, and later steps show inspector data as expected.

// REVIEWER NOTE (KOB-56322): Jira also states that a manual session inspector refresh on a slow app now shows no inspector data instead of a failed request. Confirm what users see in this case before adding it to the release note.

// Source: KOB-56380 from PR #984
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/984

== Native element searches on the iOS home screen in Xium sessions

In iOS Xium automation sessions, native element searches now find app icons on the home screen when the home screen shows widgets. Previously, an accessibility id or predicate search for an icon such as Settings could fail with a `No active application elements` error or return no matching element, and reading or tapping an icon found by XPath failed with the same error.

* Accessibility id, predicate, and XPath searches find app icons on the home screen of iPhone and iPad devices. `getAttribute`, `getRect`, and `click` work on the found element.
* Native element searches also succeed on the Wi-Fi sign-in sheet that iOS shows for captive networks.
* A native element search waits up to 5 seconds for a result instead of stopping after 500 milliseconds. A slow screen read, such as on an iPad home screen with widgets, no longer returns a missing element.

== Network payload capture setup errors on iOS

When network payload capture can't be set up at the start of an iOS session, Kobiton Portal now shows an error notification. The session stays usable but doesn't capture network traffic.

* The notification reads `Network capture setup failed. This session will run without capturing traffic.` and describes the cause and what to do next.
* Select *Details* to view the error reported by the device.
* The notification appears in manual sessions and in the live view of automation sessions, and appears again after a page reload.
* A successful setup shows no notification.
* Android devices don't show this notification.

See xref:manual-testing:local-devices/capture-network-payload-data.adoc[].

== Signing details for iOS app versions in the API

Signing details are now read from the provisioning profile of each iOS app uploaded to App Repository and returned with the app version in the Kobiton API v2.

* App version objects in API v2 responses, including an app's `latest_version` and `versions`, include a new `signing` object.
* The `signing` object summarizes the provisioning profile type, whether the profile covers all devices or how many devices it covers, the team ID, and when the profile and the latest signing certificate expire.
* Android app versions, and iOS app versions uploaded before this release, return `signing: null`.
* Device UDIDs and certificate identity details are not returned.
* Uploads work as before, including iOS apps without a provisioning profile.

== Faster recovery for iOS devices plugged back in during startup

When an iOS device on a macOS deviceConnect host is unplugged and plugged back in while deviceConnect is still bringing it online, the device now comes back online within seconds. Previously, the device could take about a minute to recover.

Unplugging an iOS device also no longer logs the closed device connection as an error or warning in the deviceConnect logs. These messages are now logged at debug level.

== Control the idle wait before taps and swipes in Xium sessions

In Xium sessions on Android and iOS devices with `kobiton:waitForIdle` set to `true`, the idle wait before each tap or swipe now lasts up to the session's `waitForIdleTimeout` value instead of a fixed 5 seconds.

* Set the value when the session starts with `appium:waitForIdleTimeout` or inside the `appium:settings` capability. If both are set, the `appium:settings` value is used.
* Change the value during the session with the Appium Settings API. Set it to `0` to skip the idle wait.
* The value is in milliseconds on both Android and iOS devices.
* When no value is set, the wait before each tap or swipe now lasts up to 10 seconds instead of 5 seconds.

Basic Appium 2 sessions are not affected.

For details, see xref:automation-testing:capabilities/available-capabilities.adoc#_waitForIdleTimeout[waitForIdleTimeout].

== ZooKeeper reliability on Standalone

Standalone deployments are better protected against ZooKeeper transaction log corruption, and administrators can recover from it with a single command.

- During an update that restarts ZooKeeper, the existing ZooKeeper instance stops before the new instance starts. Previously, both instances could briefly run against the same data, which could corrupt the newest transaction log and prevent ZooKeeper and Kafka from starting. Existing installations receive this change when they update.
- ZooKeeper is briefly unavailable during an update that restarts it. Kafka reconnects when ZooKeeper is available again.
- ZooKeeper has up to 5 minutes to start before it is restarted, so a slow startup, such as replaying a large snapshot, is not interrupted.
- If ZooKeeper fails to start with an `EOFException` on its newest transaction log, run `sudo kobictl fix zookeeper-txnlog`. The command moves the damaged log to a quarantine directory instead of deleting it, restarts ZooKeeper and Kafka, and clears a failed setup job that can otherwise stall the deployment.
- The command makes no changes when the newest transaction log is healthy. It stops and reports the problem instead of recovering automatically when the damage is in an earlier log, or when Kafka reports an inconsistent cluster ID after it restarts, because automatic recovery could lose data in those cases.

// REVIEWER NOTE (KOB-56410): The recovery runbook named in the ticket lives with the installer, not the Admin Docs. If the Admin Docs will cover the manual recovery path, add the standard Admin Docs reference line.

== Apply Ubuntu security updates with `kobictl run os-patch`

Standalone servers can apply Ubuntu security updates with `sudo kobictl run os-patch`. Packages pinned by the installed Standalone release are held during the update, so patching does not move them ahead of the versions the release requires.

- `--dry-run` lists the packages that would be held and upgraded, without making changes.
- `--yes` applies the updates without a confirmation prompt.
- Holds are released after every run, including runs that fail or are interrupted. Packages held before the run stay held.
- The hold list can be adjusted per server, for a single run or permanently.
- When a kernel or NVIDIA driver update requires a restart, the run reports it. GPU workloads fail until the server restarts.
- The run lists any package sources that could not be refreshed.

For the complete procedure, refer to the Kobiton Admin Docs. If you need access, please contact your Account Manager.

// REVIEWER NOTE (KOB-56004): Confirm the first Standalone release that includes `kobictl run os-patch`. The ticket lists no fix version.
// REVIEWER NOTE (KOB-56004): The Admin Docs page for this command is planned as separate work. Confirm it is published before this entry references it.

== Power unlocks passcode devices in the deviceConnect Console viewer

In organizations with passcode mode enabled, *Power* in the deviceConnect Console device viewer now unlocks a locked device the same way *Power* does in a Portal manual session. The lock screen appears, the device passcode is filled in automatically, and the device opens on the Home screen.

* Applies to Android, iOS, and iPadOS devices that use the organization passcode.
* In organizations without passcode mode, *Power* turns the device screen off and on, and no passcode is entered.
* *Power* in Portal manual sessions is unchanged.

== Lightning Mode on Android and iOS devices without a GEM

Manual sessions on supported Android and iOS devices can stream in Lightning Mode directly from the device, without a Graphic Extension Manager (GEM). Devices that use a GEM keep their existing stream.

* The *Video* tab in the session sidebar shows the stream codec and connection metrics.
* A session's recorded video is encoded in the codec its viewers watched in. Sessions watched in HEVC are recorded as HEVC instead of H.264. Firefox, and Chrome on a computer without HEVC decoding, can't play these recordings on the session page.

== Device sound returns after unlocking iOS devices in Lightning Mode

Addressed an issue in iOS manual sessions in Lightning Mode where device sound could stop after the device was locked with *Power* and unlocked a few seconds later. The screen came back, but the live view and the session video stayed silent for the rest of the session, and turning Lightning Mode off and on or reloading the page did not restore the sound.

Device sound now returns after each unlock, in both the live view and the session video.

== Reliable Power button unlock for passcode-enabled iOS devices in Lightning mode

In organizations that use passcode (PIN) mode, iOS manual sessions in Lightning mode now recover when you select *Power* twice. After the second *Power*, the device passcode is filled in automatically, the device unlocks, and the live view shows the device screen again.

Previously, the device could stay locked and the live view could stay black. Unlocking the device another way, such as selecting *Home* and entering the passcode, did not bring the live view back.

The live view stays dark between the first and second *Power* while the device screen is off.

On iOS devices with a passcode, the live view and the session recording now keep showing the last screen while the session is paused, for example after the device language changes. Previously, the live view showed the passcode being set up again on the device.

Taps and other input sent while the *Session paused as we check the connection. It'll resume shortly.* message is displayed are now discarded. Previously, this input was held and then ran on the device all at once when the session resumed, which could change a setting by mistake.

== Lightning mode stays on after locking an iOS device

In a manual session on an iOS device in Lightning mode, selecting *Power* to lock and wake the device no longer drops the session out of Lightning mode or leaves the live view frozen on the last app screen.

* While the device is locked, the live view shows the lock screen, and taps and swipes work, so you can unlock the device from the session.
* The Screen Broadcast prompt no longer appears repeatedly while the device is locked.
* After you unlock the device, live video resumes in Lightning mode.
* Turning *Lightning Mode* back on restores the live video stream from the device.

[NOTE]
====
If live video has to restart after the device is unlocked, the device returns to the home screen.
====

== Rotated screens keep a landscape frame in iOS Lightning Mode sessions

Addressed an issue in iOS manual sessions with *Lightning Mode* turned on where rotating the device to landscape squeezed the screen into a portrait frame. This occurred while the session streamed screenshots instead of the device's own video, for example while the device showed its lock screen after *Power* was selected.

* The live view now switches to a landscape frame at the device's aspect ratio, and back to portrait when the device rotates back.
* The *Resolution* shown on the *Video* tab follows the rotation.
* The session video in Session Explorer shows landscape parts in a landscape frame, matching the step screenshots.

== Manual sessions on iPhone Duo devices and simulators

Manual sessions on iPhone Duo devices and iPhone Duo simulators now show the screen in use and respond to input on both the cover screen and the inner screen. Previously, the session stream was black while the device was folded, and taps missed their targets while it was unfolded.

* The session stream, taps, and screenshots follow the screen in use, folded or unfolded.
* Select *Fold device* or *Unfold device* on the session toolbar to change the posture. The control appears only on foldable devices.
* *Inspector* highlights and element taps in apps line up with the screen in use.
* On a real iPhone Duo, *Rotate Screen* is disabled. On iPhone Duo simulators, *Rotate Screen* rotates the screen in use.

For details and limitations, see xref:manual-testing:foldable-devices.adoc#_iphone_duo[iPhone Duo].

== Change notifications for MCP 2026-07-28 clients

AI clients that use the MCP 2026-07-28 specification now request change notifications from the Kobiton MCP server through `subscriptions/listen`. For these clients, `subscriptions/listen` replaces the HTTP GET endpoint and the `resources/subscribe` and `resources/unsubscribe` methods.

* A client opts in to each notification type it needs: tool list changes, prompt list changes, resource list changes, and updates to subscribed resources. The server acknowledges the request with a subscription ID.
* Progress and log notifications (`notifications/progress` and `notifications/message`) continue to arrive on the response stream of the request that produced them, not on `subscriptions/listen`.
* AI clients that use earlier MCP versions are unaffected.

// REVIEWER NOTE (KOB-54413): The ticket describes `subscriptions/listen` as a long-lived stream that delivers opted-in change notifications, but the implementation plan describes it as acknowledging the request and then completing the stream. Confirm whether clients receive list-change notifications on this stream before publishing, and keep this entry limited to the acknowledgment if they do not.

// Source: KOB-54418 from PR #956
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/956

== Interrupted MCP response streams are not resumed

The Kobiton MCP server follows the MCP 2026-07-28 specification for interrupted responses. If a response stream breaks before the response is complete, the in-flight request is not resumed or redelivered.

* SSE event IDs are not sent, and the `Last-Event-ID` header is ignored.
* To recover, send the request again as a new request with a new request ID. The server handles it as an independent request.

// REVIEWER NOTE (KOB-54418): The source lists this story as verification-only under the MCP 2026-07-28 release. Confirm whether the Kobiton MCP server previously supported stream resumability. If it did not, this entry describes current behavior rather than a change and may belong with the existing MCP 2026-07-28 release-note entry instead of standing alone.

// Source: KOB-54411 from PR #955
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/955

== Kobiton MCP server supports stateless requests

The Kobiton MCP server now accepts stateless requests from MCP clients that use the MCP 2026-07-28 specification. These clients no longer need to start with an `initialize` handshake.

- Each request carries its protocol version and client capabilities in the request `_meta` field.
- Each result includes the server information in its `_meta` field.
- Requests that specify an unsupported protocol version return an `UnsupportedProtocolVersionError` error.

MCP clients that connect with the `initialize` handshake continue to work without changes.

// Source: KOB-54414 from PR #954
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/954

== Per-request logging for MCP 2026-07-28 clients

For AI clients that use version 2026-07-28 of the Model Context Protocol (MCP), log messages from the Kobiton MCP server are now controlled per request.

- Log messages are sent only for requests that set a log level in the `io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel` field of `_meta`. Requests without this field receive no log messages.
- The `ping` and `logging/setLevel` requests and the `notifications/roots/list_changed` notification are no longer supported for these clients.
- Clients that use earlier MCP versions are not affected.

// REVIEWER NOTE (KOB-54414): The Cloud November 6, 2026 release notes already announce support for MCP specification 2026-07-28. Decide whether to publish this entry separately or fold it into that existing section.
// REVIEWER NOTE (KOB-54414): The ticket description states the removal without qualification, while the ticket's Impact notes say clients that use the earlier initialization handshake keep the previous protocol. Confirm that `ping` and `logging/setLevel` still work for earlier-version clients before publishing the last bullet.

== Saving text with invalid Unicode characters

Text that contains an unpaired Unicode surrogate character no longer causes a save to fail.

* Fixed an issue where renaming a Test Suite, or saving other text, failed with a server error when the text contained an unpaired Unicode surrogate character. The text now saves, and the invalid character is stored as the Unicode replacement character (�).
* Fixed an issue where session completion and usage were not recorded for some subscriptions.

For details on editing a Test Suite, see xref:test-management:test-suites.adoc[Test Suites].

// Source: KOB-55752 from PR #952
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/952

== File push and pull commands in Xium sessions

Xium sessions on Android and iOS devices now support the `mobile: pushFile` and `mobile: pullFile` commands. Scripts that transfer files run the same way in Xium and basic Appium 2 sessions, and no longer return a `not implemented` error in Xium.

* `mobile: pushFile` saves a file to the device. Pass the destination path in `remotePath` and the Base64-encoded file content in `payload`.
* `mobile: pullFile` returns the content of the file at `remotePath`. If the file does not exist, the command returns an error.
* By default, files larger than 100 MB are refused by `mobile: pushFile`, `mobile: pullFile`, and the legacy `push_file` endpoint. The limit is set by the `WebDriverController.MaxFileTransferBytes` key in the deviceConnect `dc.ini` file.
* File push and pull through Kobiton CLI are not affected by this limit.

// REVIEWER NOTE (KOB-55752): Confirm which deployments can change the `dc.ini` limit (for example, Standalone or customer-managed deviceConnect hosts only) and that "legacy `push_file` endpoint" is the customer-recognizable name for the older push route.

// Source: KOB-55794 from PR #948
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/948

== Network capture profiles reject blank Capture Filter entries

Creating or updating a network capture profile through the Kobiton API now returns a `400` error when a *Capture Filter* entry is empty, contains only whitespace, or is `null`. The profile isn't created or changed. Valid entries, such as `*`, `kobiton.*`, and `api.kobiton.com/v2/*`, are accepted as before.

* Profiles saved with a blank *Capture Filter* entry before this change still appear in the list, open, and can be selected when starting a session.
* To save changes to one of these profiles in Kobiton Portal, remove the empty *Capture Filter* entry first. Otherwise, *Save* shows an error message and the profile isn't changed.

The published configuration page still uses "Configurations" and "base domains". Confirm the rename ships in the same release before publishing this entry.

== Launch with network capture from the device list

Launching a device with network capture from the device list now uses the same searchable profile picker as the device overview, so both launch paths behave the same way.

* The launch menu option *Use custom configuration* is now *Launch with network capture*.
* The dialog it opens is now titled *Network Capture*. Search saved profiles by name or domain, or select *+All requests *+* or *Custom*.
* Selecting *Custom* shows a *Capture Filter* field in the dialog. The session doesn't launch until you enter at least one domain.
* If the selected profile was deleted after you opened the dialog, the session doesn't launch. The dialog stays open, the selection is cleared, and a message shows that the profile no longer exists.
* The previous non-searchable dropdown is removed.

See xref:manual-testing:local-devices/capture-network-payload-data.adoc#_launch_with_network_capture_from_the_device_list[Launch with network capture from the device list].

=== Network capture settings use profile naming

The settings for network payload capture now refer to profiles instead of configurations.

* The *Configurations* tab in *Settings* is now *Network Capture*.
* The listing page title is *Network Capture Profiles*, and the add button is *Add New Profile*.
* When no profiles exist, the empty-state message references the add button that appears on the page.
* Deleting a profile shows "profile" in both the confirmation dialog and the success message.

Existing profiles remain in the list with their names unchanged. Network payload capture behavior is unchanged.

// Source: KOB-36354 from PR #945
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/945

== Network Payload Capture

* Fixed an issue where you couldn't save a new Network Payload Capture configuration if another organization already used the same configuration name. Configuration names now only need to be unique within your organization, and names that differ only by letter case are still treated as the same name.

// Source: KOB-54301 from PR #944
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/944

== Network capture profiles accept wildcard and path patterns

Network capture profiles now save the wildcard and path patterns that were previously rejected, and the profile page is simpler.

* Patterns such as `*`, `kobiton.*`, `portal.*.com`, and `api.kobiton.com/v2/*` can now be saved, so a profile can capture a whole domain or a path.
* `localhost`, single-label hostnames, and hostnames with uppercase letters are also accepted.
* The *Advanced Settings* section and its seven content-type checkboxes are removed. You no longer select content types. A profile captures the traffic that matches its filter.
* The field is now named *Capture Filter*, and the profile page is now *Network Capture Profile*. In Session Overview, the capture panel is now *Network Capture Profile*, and its column is now *Capture Filter*.
* Editing an existing profile doesn't change the content it captures.

See xref:devices:local-devices/network-payload-capture/create-a-configuration.adoc[].

// Source: KOB-56320 from PR #943

== deviceConnect runs on .NET 11

deviceConnect now runs on .NET 11 on macOS and Linux hosts.

* The macOS installer includes the .NET runtime instead of the full .NET SDK, which makes the installer about 300 MB smaller.
* Updating deviceConnect on an existing host moves it to .NET 11.

== Redrawn fold and unfold icons

The fold and unfold icons in the manual session toolbar and the Session Explorer timeline are redrawn so they are easier to recognize at 100% browser zoom.

* When the device is unfolded, the toolbar shows the new *Fold device* icon. When the device is folded, the toolbar shows the new *Unfold device* icon. Tooltips and fold behavior are unchanged.
* The toolbar icon is a darker gray, and the entire icon changes color on hover and while pressed.
* *FOLD DEVICE* and *UNFOLD DEVICE* steps in the Session Explorer timeline use the same icons.

For details, see xref:manual-testing:device-controls.adoc#_fold_or_unfold_device[Fold or unfold device].
